text:
sam: heads up — noticed a recent batch upload to archive-bucket-prod that doesn't have CMEK metadata, looks like SSE-S3 only :thinking_face:
priya: wtf, was that via the backup job or manual?
sam: backup-uploader@prod service principal. logs show it used storage.objectAdmin role from terraform module `modules/legacy-backups`
anna: we migrated backups to CMEK last quarter — wonder if the old module was re-applied during the infra cleanup?
mike: can you paste the audit log line?
sam: sure, from cloud-audit (redacted):
```
protoPayload.methodName: "storage.objects.insert"
resourceName: "projects/_/buckets/archive-bucket-prod/objects/db-snap-2026-03-21.tar.gz"
authenticationInfo.principalEmail: "backup-uploader@prod"
requestMetadata.cmekKey: null
labels: { "uploaded-by": "scheduled-backup" }
```
jen: cmekKey null => uploaded without customer-managed key. That explains the compliance alert. Did KMS deny/decrypt events show anything?
sam: weirdly CloudTrail/KMS logs don't show a Decrypt/Encrypt event for that object — looks like the uploader never attempted CMEK because it lacked kms:Encrypt permission on the key.
priya: so two issues: RBAC drift granted the uploader broad storage perms, and KMS grants were not scoped or were rotated/expired. Did we recently rotate the CMK?
anna: we did a CMK rotate last week but applied time-limited grant tokens to the backup service principal. IIRC the grant TTL was 72h for the temporary grant used during migration testing. Might have expired before a later backup run.
mike: can we confirm terraform history? maybe someone reapplied the legacy module after the rotate. @devops-bot any deploy events for `modules/legacy-backups` around 1716185000-1716200000?
devops-bot: deploy: terraform apply in org/infrastructure/legacy-backups at 1716197205 by ci-pipeline. Plan included: +google_storage_bucket_iam_binding.backup_uploader -> role: roles/storage.objectAdmin
jen: ok that confirms it. The pipeline reapplied old binding after the rotate window and that principal now uploads without KMS usage.
sam: immediate mitigation options? rollback the iam binding, or add explicit conditional binding that requires encryption?
priya: short-term: revoke the roles/storage.objectAdmin binding from backup-uploader@prod and add a granular role that only allows PutObject with kms:Encrypt enforced via bucket policy if possible. Also rotate the backup uploader key used by the pipeline credentials.
anna: we should also re-run a scan for any objects in archive-bucket-prod without cmek metadata and mark them for re-encryption or deletion. create an integrity list.
mike: query suggestion for audit logs (GCP):
```sql
SELECT protoPayload.resourceName, protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, timestamp
FROM `project.activity_logs.cloudaudit_googleapis_com_activity`
WHERE protoPayload.methodName = "storage.objects.insert"
  AND json_extract_scalar(protoPayload.request, '$.cmekKey') IS NULL
  AND timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)
```
jen: good. I'll run that and tag objects. Also add a Cloud Asset Inventory snapshot to detect any IAM bindings that reference legacy modules.
priya: long term: enforce KMS usage via org-level constraints and require iam:passRole/kms:Encrypt in CI check gates. Also add a nightly audit that cross-checks KMS grants against expected service principals and TTLs.
sam: one more gotcha — our KMS grant audit didn't surface expired grants because we only looked for explicit key policy changes, not ephemeral grants. We need to capture GrantCreate/GrantRevoke events in the monitoring alert rules.
anna: agreed. file a quick playbook update: encops-runbook.md -> add section "ephemeral grant TTL detection" with queries and runbook steps.
mike: I'll open a minimal incident ticket and assign to encops oncall. Priority P2 for now (no data exfil, but compliance gap).
jen: created INC-2026-031 — assigned to @priya and @sam, added checklist: revoke binding, rotate pipeline creds, audit objects, re-encrypt or quarantine, update runbook.
priya: starting with revoke. tagging infra for rollback: @devops-team please standby. :rotating_light:
sam: thanks — will post findings once the object scan completes.
security-bot: automated reminder: please file a post-incident runbook update within 72h. :memo:
jen: will do. quick note — we should also evaluate switching backup pipeline to use KMS-integrated uploader client library that fails uploads without CMEK header. low-effort but raises safety.
priya: agreed. adding to backlog: "backup-uploader: enforce CMEK at SDK level"
sam: scan results: found 3 objects without cmek in the last 48h, all from the same timeframe — tagging for re-encrypt.
jen: thanks. moving to next steps in INC-2026-031. we should close the slack loop once remediation verified. :white_check_mark:
